title: Adaptive telemetry gateway for mixed SDK/CLI/API schema transforms
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Build an adaptive telemetry gateway that sits between client SDK/CLI/API producers and the analytics ingestion pipeline to perform lossless schema transforms, capability negotiation, and progressive rollouts for schema versions. This gateway will enable mixed-version clients to send telemetry without requiring immediate coordinated client updates and will provide observable compatibility metrics, automated contract checks, and replay-friendly transforms for downstream consumers. The focus is on preserving event fidelity, enabling safe schema evolution, and minimizing production disruption while keeping latency impact below 10ms p50 for synchronous pathways.
background: We have multiple concurrent schema changes (field renames, optional/required shifts, typed payload migration) across SDKs, the CLI, and HTTP API clients. Current approach forces coordinated client and server upgrades or brittle ad-hoc mappers in consumers. That increases rollback risk and slows feature delivery. A lightweight, runtime gateway that implements deterministic transforms and records transform metadata will decouple producer upgrades from consumer consumption and improve incident triage.
technical_design: Handshake: clients include Capability header (Telem-Cap: sdk=v2;schema=2025-01) and optional capability JSON for fine-grained feature flags.
Descriptor Registry: centralized, versioned descriptors for event types with stable IDs and human-readable names. Registry served via the console and cdn with immutable URLs.

Transform Engine: pluggable transform functions that can do rename/copy/compute/defaults/redact. Transforms are idempotent and reversible where possible; each transform records a ledger entry (transform-id) attached to the output event.
Compatibility Scoring: gateway applies heuristics to score forward/backwards compatibility and emits metrics when a transform downgrades fidelity or drops unknown fields.
Validator: strict mode (reject events failing contract) and permissive mode (accept + transform + annotate). Admins can toggle per-project policy.
Replay/Backfill: gateway logs original payloads and transform metadata to a replay bucket for consumers to re-run transforms as descriptors evolve.
SDK/CLI Shims: lightweight client libs will surface capability headers and optional client-side validation to reduce gateway load. Non-upgraded SDKs will be handled by gateway transforms.
Observability: per-route histograms, transform failure counters, compatibility degradation alerts, sample event traces, and transform ledger query API for audits.
Performance: route hot-path implemented in Rust; transform registry cached in memory with TTL; async write to replay log to avoid blocking ingestion path.
Security/compliance: PII redaction policies available as transform stages; all replay logs encrypted with KMS-managed keys and access audited.
Rollout: canary gateway cluster + consumer contract tests before global switch; runtime feature-flag to revert to passthrough mode.
Data Contracts: define a minimal contract test suite per schema update that runs in CI and as part of canary verification.
Fallback: when transform fails and policy == permissive, gateway forwards original payload with transform-failure metadata so consumers can choose behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway accepts telemetry from SDK v1/v2 and CLI without client upgrades in mixed environment and correctly applies transforms for at least 95% of sampled events.
End-to-end p50 added latency from gateway on synchronous path <= 10ms, p95 <= 35ms under normal load.
Transform ledger stored and queryable; at least 7 days of replayable payloads available for a project by default.
Compatibility degradation metric emits an alert when a new descriptor registration causes >1% of events to be downgraded in the canary region.
Automated contract tests exist and run in canary pipeline; canary must pass before global rollout.
Manual rollback to passthrough mode tested and validated in staging and prod canary.
Documentation and SDK/CLI shim release notes published and linked from the console.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: deploy gateway as opt-in endpoint for dev projects; collect telemetry and adjust transforms.
Phase 1: enable canary for 5% of traffic (region-scoped); run compatibility scoring and contract tests.
Phase 2: after two successful canary cycles and no critical degradations, expand to 25% and run downstream consumer smoke tests.
Phase 3: full rollout with alerting and 1-hour rollback window; monitor cost and latency impacts.
Post-rollout: enable replay backfills for consumers and run a 48-hour retrospective to validate assumptions.
testing_plan: Unit + integration tests for transform library with golden fixtures covering renames, nested field moves, and type coercion.
Fuzz tests to generate unknown fields and unexpected types to evaluate perceptible data loss metrics.
Load tests simulating mixed-version clients at target QPS to validate latency SLOs and memory behavior.
Contract suite executed in CI and canary pipelines; failing test blocks canary promotion.
End-to-end shadow mode for one week: gateway mirrors transformed events to ingestion while original path continues; compare consumer outputs.
Replay validation: reprocess stored original payloads through new transforms in staging to validate consumer compatibility.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: transforms accidentally drop critical fields. Mitigation: strict unit tests + compatibility scoring + sample auditing + reversible transforms where possible.
Risk: added latency on hot paths. Mitigation: Rust hot-path, transform caching, per-project flow control and async persistence to replay store.
Risk: excessive storage cost for replay logs. Mitigation: configurable retention per project, aggregated deltas for high-volume event types.
Risk: schema registry drift produces incompatible descriptors. Mitigation: signing of descriptors, immutable URLs, and CI gating for descriptor publishing.
Risk: SDKs fail to advertise capabilities. Mitigation: graceful default of permissive transforms and telemetry metrics to identify non-compliant clients.
